structure: Part 6, Templates and address book. Read in full: e2e/templates.fit.spec.js (206 lines, 12 tests in three describe blocks: 'manage templates' 2 tests — the list and the dashboard Use template button; 'a saved template' 6 tests — view, use, change one section, POST reload plus unknown template, edit on its own task list, delete; 'create a new template' 4 tests — type then name then answers then review and save, Untitled template, discard, discard outside a template journey), e2e/address-book.fit.spec.js (220 lines, 9 tests in three describe blocks: 'address book list' 1 multi-step test — default category, page 2, the three other categories, search inside the Filter addresses disclosure; 'add an address to the address book' 6 tests — choose an address type with its error, origin or consignor by hand with errors and uses, destination/consignee/importer by search with errors and uses, branch use, transporter hand-off, the usage step guard; 'an address book entry' 2 tests — view/edit/save with error and banner, delete with banner) and the shared helper e2e/support/journey.js (270 lines: the /design-release-2.1 mount, url/urlFor, the action-button and submit helpers, expectHeading, expectErrorSummary with its 'There is a problem' title, expectBackLink, answerOrigin and answerCommodity used by the template-creation test). Every path below is under the /design-release-2.1 mount. Claims cover each route, title, heading, caption, label, hint, option, error message verbatim, banner, back link, redirect and count the 21 tests assert; journey.js is claimed only where these two specs call it. Gaps record what the tests leave unasserted (template-name validation, the address usage step with an address pending, add-address success banner, the address view page's delete link, button text on the review and edit forms).
